title: In Revelation 22 How Should The Promise Of Christs Imminent Return Affect Our Daily Lives And Priorities As Believers
paragraphs: The Promise of Christ’s Imminent Return in Revelation 22: Implications for Our Daily Lives and Priorities

Revelation 22, the final chapter of Scripture, offers a climactic vision of hope, restoration, and the imminent return of Jesus Christ. For believers, the repeated promise “I come quickly” serves not only as a source of comfort but as a call to holy living and purposeful priorities. Let’s explore how this promise is meant to shape our daily walk.
1. Living with Expectancy and Hope
Three times in Revelation 22, Jesus declares His imminent return:
And behold, I come quickly. Blessed is he that keepeth the words of the prophecy of this book. - Revelation 22:7 ASV
And behold, I come quickly; and my reward is with me, to render to each man according as his work is. - Revelation 22:12 ASV
He who testifieth these things saith, Yea: I come quickly. Amen: come, Lord Jesus. - Revelation 22:20 ASV
The certainty and nearness of Christ’s return infuse believers with hope for the future. This hope is not passive waiting but active anticipation—rooted in the faithfulness of God’s Word (John 14:3).
2. Motivated Toward Holiness and Obedience

The imminent return of Jesus is presented as a motivation to “keepeth the words of the prophecy of this book.” This means prioritizing obedience to Scripture and aligning our lives with Christ’s teaching.
And every one that hath this hope set on him purifieth himself, even as he is pure. - 1 John 3:3 ASV
Knowing that Jesus could return at any moment encourages us to pursue holiness, avoid complacency, and live with integrity.
3. Faithful Stewardship and Eternal Perspective

Jesus’ words remind us that He is coming “with my reward... to render to each man according as his work is” (Revelation 22:12). This highlights the importance of faithful stewardship—using our time, gifts, and resources for God’s purposes.
Set your mind on the things that are above, not on the things that are upon the earth. - Colossians 3:2 ASV
When we live with eternity in view, our priorities shift from temporary pursuits to investments that have everlasting significance (see also Matthew 6:19-21).
4. Urgency in Witness and Mission
The final invitation of Scripture is evangelistic:
And the Spirit and the bride say, Come. And he that heareth, let him say, Come. And he that is athirst, let him come: he that will, let him take the water of life freely. - Revelation 22:17 ASV

Believers are called to extend the invitation of salvation to others, knowing that time is short. The reality of Christ’s return should create urgency in sharing the gospel and praying for the lost (Matthew 28:19-20).
5. Endurance Amid Trials

Revelation was originally written to persecuted believers, reminding them that ultimate victory belongs to Christ. The promise of His return gives us strength to persevere, knowing that suffering is temporary and glory awaits (Romans 8:18).
Conclusion: Living in Light of His Soon Return

The promise “I come quickly” is both comfort and challenge. It calls us to live with hope, pursue holiness, steward our lives wisely, share the gospel boldly, and endure faithfully. May our daily priorities reflect the reality that we are a people awaiting our King.
